source.author: lucr
source.text: cedit item retro, de terra quod fuit ante, in terras, et quod missumst ex aetheris oris, id rursum caeli rellatum templa receptant.
source.text_original: cedit item retro, de terra quod fuit ante, / in terras, et quod missumst ex aetheris oris, / id rursum caeli rellatum templa receptant.
source.text_english: Likewise, whatever before had gone from the earth retreats back into the earth, and whatever has been sent from the regions of the sky, the temples of heaven receive it back again when it has been brought home.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: denique idem Lucretius oblitus quid assereret et quod dogma defenderet, hos uersus posuit: cedit item retro, de terra quod fuit ante, in terram, sed quod missum est ex aetheris oris, id rursum caeli fulgentia templa receptant.
reuse.text_original: denique idem Lucretius oblitus quid assereret et quod dogma defenderet, hos uersus posuit: cedit item retro, de terra quod fuit ante, in terram, sed quod missum est ex aetheris oris, id rursum caeli fulgentia templa receptant.
reuse.text_english: Finally, Lucretius himself, forgetting what he was asserting and what doctrine he was defending, set down these lines: likewise that which before came from the earth yields back again to the earth, but that which was sent from the borders of the aether the shining temples of heaven receive once more.
